Aaron Jones Sr. got banged up during the Week 7 game against the Colts, but Mason is the more every-down back who can handle more carries between the tackles. As a result, the hope is that he provides a more consistent presence on the ground. On the other side, the Lions have struggled a little bit to stop the run this season. Detroit ranks 25th in the NFL in EPA per rush allowed (-0.01). While Mason isn’t known for creating a ton of yards on his own, the Lions are allowing the fourth-most yards before contact per rush (1.77) in the league, so Minnesota should be able to create some easy yards on the ground on early downs. If it can’t, O’Connell and company have bigger problems. The passing game gets a lot of the headlines, both good and bad, in Minnesota. That makes sense considering all the big names on the team are involved with the passing game. But O’Connell is still running the Shanahan-McVay offense at its core, and the running game is essential to making the offense go. Week 8 is a perfect time for the Vikings to figure that part of things out. Can Kyler Murray get after a vulnerable Lions secondary? The Lions’ secondary has been a massive weakness this year, and most offenses have been able to throw the ball all over the yard against them. Detroit ranks 28th in EPA per pass allowed (+0.17) this season, and it is giving up the most passing yards per game among any team in the NFL. Injuries in the secondary play a part in that, but the Lions have a major weakness at cornerback even when healthy that can be exploited by a talented receiving corps like Minnesota’s. Unfortunately for the Vikings, that crop of weapons hasn’t resulted in an elite passing game so far this year. The Vikings currently rank 23rd in EPA per pass this season (-0.13) and tied for 24th in yards per passing play (5.4). Injuries to Kyler Murray, Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison at different points in the year contribute to those struggles, but the numbers should still be better than that with this amount of talent. If there’s going to be a week where the Vikings get back on track, it’s this one. The Lions, while doing okay against tight ends and running backs this season, have been getting torched by wide receivers from all alignments. Detroit is allowing the most EPA per play against slot targets (+0.70) in the NFL this season by a massive margin, and it ranks just 30th against targets to outside receivers (+0.39). Jefferson has taken more than 83% of his snaps from out wide this season, per PFF, which would match him up with D.J. Reed on a frequent basis in this one. When opponents have targeted Reed in 2026, they have had plenty of success. He has allowed the second-highest passer rating when targeted among defensive backs with at least 200 coverage snaps this season, per Next Gen Stats. His total target EPA of 27.0 is the second-worst mark in the NFL, and Jefferson is the type of receiver that can give him fits. Addison also plays primarily on the outside, but he has taken 56 reps from the slot this season. He could be the guy O’Connell decides to go to in order to exploit the Lions’ weakness against slot players. One thing that could help the Lions in this game is the return of Brian Branch . Branch made his season debut in Week 7 against the Packers after tearing his Achilles last season, finishing with four tackles, one pass breakup and an interception. Coincidence or not, the Lions allowed their fewest total yards in a game in Week 7 with Branch back in the lineup, and Sunday was their second-lowest EPA per play allowed of the season. That came against a dangerous Packers offense that can create a ton of explosive plays down the field, so maybe the Lions can continue to turn things around against the Vikings. Branch plays a lot of deep safety, which should help the Lions prevent some of those big plays down the field. But he also lines up in the nickel a lot, which will help them improve against those slot targets that have troubled them so much this season. How much he plays into this game, and how the Vikings skew their passing attack away from him, will help dictate how the game goes on Sunday afternoon. item.title: Mavericks exercise 4th year option on Zaccharie Risacher
item.description: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images Mavericks exercise 4th year option on Zaccharie Risacher appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Dallas Mavericks swung a big trade in the offseason when they acquired former No. 1 overall pick Zaccharie Risacher , who had fallen out of favor with the Atlanta Hawks. The Mavericks had a team option for the fourth year of Risacher’s rookie contract, and they decided to pick that option up , as per ClutchPoints’ NBA insider Brett Siegel, guaranteeing that he remains on the Mavericks roster at least through next season. With the Mavericks picking up Zaccharie Risacher ’s contract option for 2027-28, he will on pace to potentially hit restricted free agency the 2028 offseason. This year is a fresh start for the French native who was the NBA Draft’s top pick in 2024. After a solid rookie season with the Hawks in 2024-25, Risacher took a step backwards last year, and by the time the playoffs rolled around, he was largely out of the rotation. He appeared in only three games of the Hawks’ opening round playoff loss to the New York Knicks at a little over seven minutes per game. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Risacher had a strong preseason with the Mavericks, and he’s been a staple in new head coach Dusty May’s rotation to begin the year. He‘s played in all four of the team’s games thus far, including one start, at just about 30 minutes per game. He’s averaged 8.0 points, 6.0 rebounds, 1.5 assists, 2.0 steals and 2.0 blocked shots with splits of 30.8 percent shooting from the free-throw line, 17.6 percent shooting from the 3-point line and 83.3 percent shooting from the free-throw line. The Mavericks have begun the 2026-27 season at 2-2 and are looking to add to their win column amid a game against the Oklahoma City Thunder on Wednesday. item.title: Connecticut basketball star Abdou Toure signs with Rod Wave's Mainstay Sports Agency
item.description: FAYETTEVILLE, ARKANSAS - OCTOBER 24: Abdou Toure #1 of the Arkansas Razorbacks claps for this team during a game against the Gonzaga Bulldogs at Bud Walton Arena on October 24, 2026 in Fayetteville, Arkansas. The Razorbacks defeated the Bulldogs 76-72. (Photo by Wesley Hitt/Getty Images) (Wesley Hitt/Getty Images) Connecticut native Abdou Toure signed with Mainstay Sports Agency for marketing and brand representation on Wednesday. The firm was launched by popular rapper and Grammy nominee Rodarius Marcell Green, better known as Rod Wave. Toure starred at Notre Dame-West Haven, averaging 24.6 points and seven rebounds per game as a senior. He was recognized as a consensus five-star prospect and the Allen Iverson High School Player of the Year. According to 247Sports, he was the top-ranked recruit in Connecticut in the 2026 class. Toure chose Arkansas over interest from in-state UConn . He quickly becomes one of the agency's most accomplished clients. Rod Wave launched the firm in August under his larger Mainstay umbrella, which also includes a touring division that promoted Ye's two SoFi Stadium concerts earlier this year. The two shows grossed $32.6 million, and Rod Wave said he believed a Ye show at SoFi was the biggest hip-hop concert ever by sales. Toure joins three-time Olympic medalist Will Claye, Kenxton Perkins, the son of former NBA center Kendrick Perkins, and four-star Houston commit Oneal Delancy. Toure enrolled at the New Haven Catholic school as a relatively under-the-radar freshman. He started on the bench before earning a starting role a few games into the season. The 6-foot-5 wing earned second-team All-South Connecticut Conference honors as a freshman and drew regional recruiting interest, receiving offers from Yale, Bryant and Rutgers. But he resisted calls to join a more visible prep school and remained loyal to the Green Knights. Notre Dame went 74-6 across Toure's three seasons, winning two state championships. He finished with 1,981 career points, a program record. Signing with Rod Wave's agency is another forward-thinking move for the young basketball star. Pete Novak's New Haven-based Goatville Apparel unveiled the Toure Collection late last year, and the 19-year-old has around 60,000 TikTok followers. Toure looked fully prepared for the college game over the weekend, when Arkansas played Gonzaga in its first public exhibition game of the season. He came off the bench and scored nine points, grabbed four rebounds and blocked a shot in the Razorbacks' 76-72 win. Sign up for the Connecticut Briefing from CT Insider. item.title: Alonso on Estevao’s lack of game time and Lacroix injury worry after Chelsea’s Carabao Cup exit
item.description: Alonso on Estevao’s lack of game time and Lacroix injury worry after Chelsea’s Carabao Cup exit Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso insists Estevao will get his chance despite the Brazilian failing to feature in the Carabao Cup defeat to Liverpool. Chelsea supporters were heard singing Estevao’s name during the game, but Alonso opted not to introduce him from the bench as the Blues crashed out of the competition on penalties following a 1-1 draw. “The fans were saying a lot of things,” Alonso said. “Well, we have started with Pedro, with Danny and with Morgan up front. The game had very intense moments. We knew that it was going to be physical. “And after we had to deal with Moi, he had little problems. Malo, as well, he had cramps. So we were a little bit forced with substitutions. “And now we know that the season is going to be long. And there will be moments for everyone.” Asked whether he was seeing enough from Estevao in training, Alonso admitted the winger would understandably want more opportunities. “I understand his situation and that he could be happier for sure,” he said. “Every player wants to play, wants to be part of the team. “We have had some intense games and there will be moments for everything. I’m sure that Este will have his moment. It’s my responsibility and we need to deal with that.” Alonso also pointed to the physical demands of English football and Estevao’s recovery from injury when explaining his limited minutes. “Yes, we know that the Premier League and the game in England is really intense,” he said. “You need to be up for it. Este has played, for sure, it’s his second season. But he had the injury and he’s in that process. “Trust me, I’m sure the season is going to be long and Este is going to play his role.” Chelsea were also handed a potential injury concern during the defeat, with Maxence Lacroix suffering a hamstring problem. “Too early to tell,” Alonso said. “Probably he felt something on the hamstrings. And we need a couple of days to check what’s going to be the injury.”

item.title: Titans claim ex-Raiders franchise record holder off waivers
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Titans claim ex-Raiders franchise record holder off waivers appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Tennessee Titans have claimed defensive tackle Jonah Laulu off waivers from the Las Vegas Raiders, the team announced Wednesday. To make room for Laulu, Tennessee waived defensive tackle Timmy Horne. Laulu was released by Las Vegas on Tuesday . The 26-year-old Laulu had fallen out of the Raiders’ regular rotation this season. He recorded five tackles, three quarterback hits and half a sack across 110 defensive snaps and 24 special-teams snaps in five games. His playing time decreased after he had started 15 games for Las Vegas during the 2025 season. Despite his limited opportunities this year, Laulu brings considerable experience. He appeared in 39 games for the Raiders, including 22 starts, accumulating 91 tackles, 5.5 sacks, eight passes defended and 12 quarterback hits. He also set a franchise record with 86 tackles by a defensive lineman over his first two seasons with the team. The move gives the Titans an experienced defensive tackle ahead of Sunday’s Week 8 matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals . item.title: WPL 2027 auction: From Chamari Athapaththu to Uma Chetry, five big names left unsold
item.description: The Women's Premier League (WPL) 2027 mini-auction in Kochi saw several prominent international cricketers and familiar domestic names fail to attract bids despite their experience and previous performances. With limited slots available across five franchises, teams had to prioritise their remaining budgets and specific squad requirements. The absence of bids for several established players highlighted the intense competition for places in the league. Chamari Athapaththu — Sri Lanka Sri Lanka captain Chamari Athapaththu was among the most notable names to go unsold. The experienced all-rounder entered the auction with a base price of Rs 30 lakh but failed to attract a bid. Athapaththu featured for UP Warriorz in the 2024 WPL season, scoring 28 runs and taking four wickets in four matches. She also went unsold at the 2026 mega-auction, making this another setback for the Sri Lankan star. Sophia Dunkley — England England batter Sophia Dunkley was another high-profile omission. Listed at a base price of Rs 50 lakh, she was among the players in the highest price bracket but failed to find a buyer. Known for her aggressive top-order batting, Dunkley entered the auction as an experienced international option. However, competition for overseas slots and franchises' specific squad requirements may have influenced the outcome. Saika Ishaque — India Saika Ishaque's omission was particularly notable given her impact in Mumbai Indians' title-winning 2023 campaign. The left-arm spinner claimed 15 wickets in her debut WPL season and earned an India call-up following her performances. Despite that impressive start, Ishaque went unsold at her base price of Rs 30 lakh in Kochi, leaving her without a franchise contract for the upcoming season. Uma Chetry — India Uma Chetry is the only member of India’s 2025 Women’s World Cup-winning squad to miss out on a WPL contract. While the 24-year-old wicketkeeper-batter is yet to establish herself as a power-hitter in the T20 format, she has considerable room to develop and offers valuable skills behind the stumps. Titas Sadhu — India India pacer Titas Sadhu was another familiar name left unsold. A member of India's victorious 2023 ICC Under-19 Women's T20 World Cup squad, the Bengal seamer is known for her ability to generate swing.

item.title: 49ers release struggling cornerback Jack Jones. What's the next move at that position?
item.description: Cornerback Jack Jones, shown breaking up a pass during a game against the Broncos on Oct. 4, had a rough outing for the 49ers on Sunday in Atlanta. On Wednesday, he was released by the team. (Stephen Lam/S.F. Chronicle) The San Francisco 49ers made an unsurprising roster announcement Wednesday afternoon, followed by a somewhat more surprising one. To make room for defensive tackle DeForest Buckner, whom the 49ers acquired from the Indianapolis Colts for a 2027 fourth-round pick, the team released cornerback Jack Jones. The decision to move on from Jones shouldn't come as a shock. He struggled Sunday against the Atlanta Falcons and at times in previous weeks. In 17 coverage snaps against Atlanta, the 28-year-old allowed four catches for 39 yards on five targets. He also committed two penalties, including a costly defensive pass interference penalty on 3rd-and-8 early in the fourth quarter. Jones was benched two snaps later. Jones only played against the Falcons in the first place because nickel back Upton Stout remained out with a shoulder injury. After safety Ashtyn Davis failed in the slot to start the game, defensive coordinator Raheem Morris moved Deommodore Lenoir there. Needing a second outside corner, Morris gave Jones a shot. How bad was Jones? Bad enough that head coach Kyle Shanahan chose to insert Ephesians Prysock for his first NFL action late in a non-blowout. "We were just frustrated with some of the penalties," Shanahan said when asked about playing Prysock. What makes the move semi-shocking: By releasing Jones, San Francisco is left with three healthy outside cornerbacks in Renardo Green, Lenoir and Prysock. The 49ers have a few options. With the Nov. 10 trade deadline approaching, they could pursue another boundary cornerback who would give them the option to move Lenoir inside more regularly if Stout's shoulder injury continues to linger. Or the 49ers could trust that Stout will return to his early-season form after the bye week. In that scenario, San Francisco could look to activate Nate Hobbs from injured reserve. Hobbs has been out all season with a groin injury he suffered in August. The 49ers signed Hobbs, 27, in March after he spent one season with the Green Bay Packers. Before that, he played his first four NFL seasons with the Las Vegas Raiders, starting 38 of 51 games. Hobbs brings some inside-outside versatility at 6 feet, 195 pounds. He spent more than 75% of his snaps on the outside with Green Bay. With the Raiders in 2023 and 2024, he played the majority of his snaps in the slot. Asked about the possibility of Hobbs playing nickel in Stout's absence on Oct. 5, Shanahan said: "He can be an option, too. Got to see exactly where his rehab's at. I know he's getting close, but that would be an option also." Hobbs missed 16 games from 2022-2024 due to a broken hand and multiple ankle issues. item.title: Monitoring the weather for Notre Dame VS Miami
item.description: SOUTH BEND, IN - NOVEMBER 08: A general view of Notre Dame Stadium as the snow falls during the game between the Navy Midshipmen and the Notre Dame Fighting Irish on November 08, 2025 at Notre Dame Stadium in South Bend, IN. (Photo by Joseph Weiser/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images One of the great joys about being a northern college football team is when a school from the south has to come up north in November to play a game. On November 7, the No. 1 ranked Miami Hurricanes will come up to South Bend to face the No. 5 Notre Dame Fighting Irish in a game that has been wildly anticipated since Notre Dame’s loss to Miami in the 2025 season opener. We knew both teams would come into this game highly ranked with National Championship hopes (somewhat) on the line, and it’s lining up to be a good one with the Irish currently holding an early favorite line of -3.5. But back to the southern teams coming up north… what about the weather? While our hopes are always that it’s really cold for this type of game, the truth is that for the first weekend in November in South Bend… it’s typically fairly nice and even somewhat mild (last year’s Navy game was on the 2nd Saturday of November). This year we are getting an early forecast of… it’s fine. While its should be fairly cold come kickoff for the prime time matchup, it’s not like it will be freezing with rain and/or snow. It’s going to be football weather in South Bend. Now, again, this is an early forecast and it could likely change over the coming days. Because it’s early, it’s not a bad idea to see what the weather is on the bookends of that Saturday. So… it could be a bit wetter and/or a bit warmer depending upon atmospheric shifts. You know… just something to monitor.

item.title: Match Report: Bayern Munich 6-1 FC Magdeburg
item.description: (Photo by F. Noever/FC Bayern via Getty Images) | FC Bayern via Getty Images Bayern Munich defeated second-tier side FC Magdeburg 6-1 in the second round of the DFB-Pokal on Wednesday. After some early drama, Bayern — still missing head coach Vincent Kompany after his recent hospitalization and dealing with numerous injury absences—settled in and cruised on a jubilant evening at the Allianz Arena. Recently crowned Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane enjoyed a night off as a heavily rotated side under interim manager Aaron Danks prepared for this weekend’s huge Der Klassiker against level-on-points Borussia Dortmund. It was a game that featured both new acquisitions and rising youngsters. Ismael Sai bari flashed brilliance and composure in front of goal to get the scoring started, darting into the box and laying off to Michael Olise to tap in a 10th-minute opening goal. However, before Bayern could rest easy—and bring on the academy talent — Magdeburg fired a warning shot and then some through a stupendous strike from outside the box by Mateusz Żukowski just five minutes later. The shot, which came earlier than expected and also deflected off defender Hiroki Itō, left Bayern keeper Jonas Urbig rooted to the spot. Saibari soon restored the Bayern advantage, however, this time with Olise as the suppl ier. Another lively run into the box, another cutting ball played through the defensive lines, and this time capped off with a well-placed chip over goalkeeper Dominik Reimann. The visitors gave a good account of themselves throughout the first half, even striking the post just before halftime. But Bayern kept the one-goal a dvantage heading into the break and exploded out of the gates afterward. Can adian left-back/winger Alphonso Davies entered for forward Serge Gnabry and proved to be an instant impact. By the 50th minute, he had won a penalty—coolly lofted home by Michael Olise from the spot in Kane’s absence—and followed tha t up with a quick-fire goal (70’) and assist (73’). Bayern’s 18-year-old maestro Lennart Karl provided the incisive pass on the first of those, and summer signing Nathaniel Brown, who like Davies continues to defy positional pigeon-holing despite being a nominal left-back, s crambled in the second. It was a passing showcase for Bayern, who despite Magdeburg’s c ompact shape were able to cut through time and again, particularly in the second half. And if this has bee n an uneven sophomore campaign for Karl to date, this was a night for the young man to answer his critics . Bayern got a glimpse at the future, too. Two promising youngsters, Tim Binder (75’) and David Santos Dai ber (82’), were afforded extended cameo ap pearances on account of the scoreline. Santos Daiber got on the scoresheet himself with a sizzling shot from range as stoppage time ticked away. item.title: Dick Vitale is ‘full speed ahead’ to call games this college basketball season
item.description: Credit: Jay Biggerstaff-USA TODAY Sports After a number of health-related setbacks have kept Dick Vitale limited in his appearances behind the microphone in recent years, the beloved ESPN college basketball commentator is “full speed ahead” as the season prepares to tip off next week, according to a report in the East County Observer , a local newspaper based in Lakewood Ranch, where Vitale lives. Vitale is currently undergoing his fifth cancer treatment in six years , this time for melanoma that he was diagnosed with earlier this year. But in spite of the obstacles, Vitale made his return to broadcasting in a limited capacity last season, even calling a First Four game alongside Charles Barkley , the first NCAA Tournament game Vitale has called in his storied career. Per Jay Heater in the Observer , Vitale sees calling games as one of the best ways he can battle cancer. “It’s not easy battling cancer,” he told Heater. “There is lots of chemo and radiation. But I always think positive, and I have faith. If you don’t, cancer will eat you alive. My advice is to stay active. If you do nothing, lay in bed, it will eat you up.” Vitale will call his first game of the season when North Carolina and West Virginia meet on Nov. 27 from the Spectrum Center in Charlotte, NC, for the Dick Vitale Invitational. It’s unclear how expansive his schedule will be this season, but Vitale says if he couldn’t perform up to his standards, he wouldn’t accept the assignments. “You need to have that energy and enthusiasm,” he said. “So I won’t accept any project unless I can finish it. If I can’t be me, I won’t accept that assignment.” Vitale’s contract with ESPN runs through the 2027-28 season; he’ll have served at the network for 48 years at the conclusion of his deal. item.title: Golf course in Vietnam will host 2027 Asia-Pacific Amateur Championship
item.description: One of the pathways to the Masters is going to Vietnam for the first time. The Masters Tournament, the R&A and the Asia-Pacific Golf Confederation announced Wednesday that Hoiana Shores in Hoi An, Vietnam, will host the 2027 Asia-Pacific Amateur Championship. This marks the first time this premier amateur event, which affords the winner an invitation to the following year's Masters, will be played in Vietnam. The 2027 event will be the 18th edition of the Asia-Pacific Amateur Championship. It was also announced that the 2028 tournament will be played at New South Wales in Sydney, Australia, a course also hosting for the first time. “We are very fortunate to be able to stage the Asia-Pacific Amateur Championship at some of the world’s finest courses and Hoiana Shores and New South Wales are undoubtedly in that category. “We are very much looking forward to taking the championship to Vietnam for the first time and enjoying one of the world’s great emerging golf destinations," said Mark Darbon, Chief Executive of The R&A, in a statement released by the three governing bodies. "We are also thrilled to be returning to Australia and visiting such a renowned championship venue as New South Wales for the first time." Hoiana Shores was designed by Robert Trent Jones Jr. and opened in 2019. The golf course has views of the South China Sea and the Cham Islands and was built along more than 1½ miles of beachfront sand dunes. Todd Kelly is the assistant managing editor for Golfweek. item.title: Arsenal Must Sign Another Attacker in January – Opinion
item.description: Arsenal Must Sign Another Attacker in January – Opinion Even before it was revealed that Bukayo Saka would be injured for a couple of months, Andrea Berta was under pressure to improve our attack this January. Yet we said the same in the summer , and the Italian somehow made us weaker in that department. By selling Trossard, Jesus and Martinelli, loaning out Nwaneri and replacing them only with Tzolis, the champions have fewer attacking options than this time last year. Quite incredible when, for months, most in the sport knew that was the area our squad needed improving. If the target was to help Arsenal get over the line in the Champions League, making the weakest part of our team weaker is either arrogant, naive or both. It’s not like we were under financial pressure to raise funds, so it was a gamble our recruitment team didn’t need to make. Questions for Andrea Berta Our Director of Football surely watches football? Therefore, he would know that it’s been a few seasons since Saka didn’t have a spell on the sidelines? You assume the 54-year-old communicates with Mikel Arteta? Therefore, he would know that the Spaniard clearly doesn’t trust Viktor Gyökeres and is losing faith in Eze. Remember, Mr Berta isn’t doing us any favours. It’s literally his job! He gets paid thousands of pounds a week to put together a shortlist to improve the team. There are two months a year to negotiate with other clubs, but that doesn’t stop him scouting and identifying talent in between so that list is ready for January. Yet two years ago, our manager made it clear that he was short of numbers up front and asked for help, help that never arrived. While no one at the Emirates would admit it, it was the definition of waving the white flag in the title race. It was insulting to our fanbase to pretend that we could challenge for honours with a midfielder (Merino) as a makeshift striker, Sterling on loan and a full-back as an attacking sub. It would be equally insulting to pretend that we currently have enough firepower to be champions of Europe. (Photo by Alex Grimm/Getty Images) Arsenal Cannot Afford to Stand Still Kai Havertz, who has never been and never will be a natural goalscorer, Madueke, whose final ball is terrible, and a player still needing to settle into a new culture. There is hope that Dowman will be given more opportunities, but the best team in England shouldn’t be relying on a 16-year-old for creativity. You wouldn’t put it past the Gunners to be top of the league in the New Year and think they can get away with what they have, especially if it’s confirmed Man City have been deducted points. There are Gooners who think the definition of a supporter is to only say positive things about the team they love. They will follow the company line that the policy is to only sign individuals who make us better and that they don’t exist in the winter. To be a big club, you think like a big club. Many title winners don’t respond by reducing their offensive options

item.title: Marquette Volleyball Preview: vs Creighton & vs DePaul
item.description: What an odd four days for Marquette volleyball. They’re going to play Creighton and DePaul, in that order. item.title: Police reveal disturbing allegations in Edgar Berlanga battery arrest
item.description: NEW YORK, NEW YORK - JULY 26: Edgar Berlanga in action during their Super Middleweight bout Steven Butler at Infosys Theater at Madison Square Garden on July 26, 2026 in New York City. (Photo by Evan Bernstein/Getty Images) | Getty Images New details have emerged regarding the allegations against Zuffa Boxing super middleweight Edgar Berlanga following his arrest in Florida. Berlanga was arrested Monday by the Lakeland Police Department and charged with one count of first-degree misdemeanor domestic battery and one count of second-degree felony aggravated battery involving a deadly weapon. The charges stem from an alleged Oct. 18 altercation with Genesis Maria Calderon , who is identified in a sworn police complaint affidavit as the mother of Berlanga’s child. According to the affidavit obtained by TMZ Sports , Calderon told investigators that she and Berlanga were traveling in a vehicle when an argument began. Calderon alleged that Berlanga struck her multiple times with an open hand before removing a pistol from a cupholder and hitting her in the forehead with the magazine well of the firearm. Calderon told police that she attempted to exit the vehicle, but Berlanga allegedly grabbed her left arm and attempted to pull her back inside. She eventually escaped and ran toward a nearby 7-Eleven, where bystanders contacted law enforcement. The investigating officer reported observing swelling and bruising on Calderon’s forehead. The officer also documented a torn shirt sleeve and an apparent bruise on her left inner arm. Calderon told investigators that the firearm was real and said she had witnessed Berlanga fire it at a gun range approximately 20 minutes before the alleged incident. Berlanga appeared before a judge by video Tuesday. His bail was set at a combined $16,000, and his arraignment is scheduled for Nov. 17. Neither Berlanga nor Zuffa Boxing has publicly addressed the allegations as of this writing. For more boxing news and notes click here .

item.description: It is time to celebrate Stan Wawrinka’s tennis career. The Swiss superstar saw his legendary tennis career come to an end on Tuesday evening following defeat to Jiri Lehecka in the Basel Open first round. “For me, it’s an ideal ending,” Wawrinka told reporters in Switzerland after the 5-7, 6-7 defeat on Centre Court. Following Wawrinka’s retirement, let’s take a look back at some of his greatest moments as a tennis player. 2014 Australian Open Wawrinka became the first and only man in tennis history to defeat Novak Djokovic and Rafael Nadal en route to a Grand Slam title when he won the 2014 Australian Open. The Swiss superstar – who also defeated Andrey Golubev, Alejandro Falla, Vasek Pospisil, Tommy Robredo and Tomas Berdych at the event – defeated Djokovic 2-6, 6-4, 6-2 3-6, 9-7 in the quarter-finals. Wawrinka went on to defeat Berdych in the last four, setting up a final clash with world number one Rafael Nadal. Wawrinka proved too strong for Nadal, who struggled with a back injury and a blistered hand, triumphing 6-3, 6-2, 3-6, 6-3 inside Rod Laver Arena. “I still think that I’m dreaming,” said Wawrinka afterwards. “It’s a strange feeling. I saw so many finals. I always try to watch the finals of Grand Slams because that’s where the best players are playing. “Before today, for me it wasn’t a dream. I never expected to play a final. I never expected to win a Grand Slam. And right now I just did it.” 2015 Roland Garros Around 17 months later, Wawrinka snagged his second Grand Slam crown. Wawrinka, seeded eighth in Paris, defeated Djokovic to win the major title for the first time. “It was an incredible atmosphere on court and I felt emotion like I never have before,” said Wawrinka after winning 4-6, 6-4, 6-3, 6-4 on Court Philippe Chatrier. item.description: Tottenham Hotspur Women dismantled WSL2 side Bristol City in the Players Cup thanks to a Shekiera Martinez hattrick. The comprehensive win takes us to 6th place in the Subway Players’ cup table. Martin Ho sent out a largely rotated side. Most notably, Hanna Wijk came into the side for a rare start. Side note, but it was also nice to see our former academy player (and known Spurs fan) Esther Morgan starting for Bristol City. I’ll always have a soft spot for her. In the opening stages, the side looked, well , very much like a side who’d lost three consecutive league games. We looked in danger of succumbing to Bristol City’s high press and totally unable to string anything together. But then Amanda Nildén remembered who she was and dribbled through half of Bristol City’s team before playing a pass over the top to release Shekiera Martinez. Shekiera offered up a lovely chipped finish, and that was it – we were on the sheet. From there, Bristol fell apart. Their defense made the fatal error of leaving Olivia Holdt open in the middle of the box, and it was easy for Kirsty Hanson to find her on the cross. A nice team move resulted in Shekiera Martinez’s second goal – another tap-in from dead range. For some variety, Signe Gaupest scored our fourth on a smart long range shot after Bristol tried to play out from the back. Spurs’ concentration momentarily lapsed after that, and a miscontrol by Hanna Wijk in the box ultimately led to Bristol grabbing one back. But let’s be serious, I’m not really going to complain about going to complain going into halftime 4-1. Bristol City are fourth in the WSL2 and although they look to be well coached, they’re simply not very good. And fair enough, not many WSL teams are going to leave players totally unmarked in the middle of their box. We need practice against very pressy sides, and we certainly got that. They’re definitely going to be a bit of a respite from the top of the table talent we’ve been facing. But Birmingham City do have the excellent Océane Hurtré, who’s shown she can score at pretty much any time. Ideally, though, we’ll be able to keep momentum going and continue to build back our confidence.

item.title: ‘You are a proverbial sitting duck’: Clay Travis understands Pat McAfee’s fear after Charlie Kirk’s assassination
item.description: Credit: College GameDay on ESPN The University of Utah shared a video of students poking fun at McAfee ahead of last Saturday’s College GameDay , and the former kicker fired back on the broadcast , picking against the Utes and telling the crowd that he hoped he’d never see them again. On Monday’s episode of The Pat McAfee Show, he admitted tthat he felt uncomfortable on campus and even called back to the assassination of Charlie Kirk at Utah Valley University. On Wednesday, Clay Travis posted a video to social media explaining why he feels McAfee’s stance is completely reasonable. “I think Pat McAfee’s fear that with the ratcheting up of negativity, with the fact that everyone who has a job like mine, like his, we regularly get serious death threats. We had security outside of my house for the 2024 election because people were sending mailed death threats to my house saying they were going to kill me and counting down the days until they could do it,” Travis said. I understand where Pat McAfee is coming from. I’ve received serious death threats that required armed security at my home. During Super Bowl week in 2018, I remember broadcasting live and realizing we were sitting ducks. Most people have no idea how vulnerable we are. https://t.co/bBKwBqoYHH — Clay Travis (@ClayTravis) October 28, 2026 “We now live behind a lot of armed security for that exact reason. I think that in the wake of Charlie Kirk, it is eminently reasonable for Pat McAfee to have that concern… “Anybody who sits on a desk like that in a public venue, it is hard not to think about somebody deciding to engage in terror while there is live television going on, or in the case of the radio show, while there is Um, while there is live radio going on. And people may say, ‘Clay, why do you mention this? It’s a dark thought.’ “It’s 100% correct, it is a dark thought. But Pat McAfee has brought it up, and I’ve actually seen a lot of people saying, ‘suck it up, stop whining.’ Uh, I actually think his fear there is 100% justified. And I believe he said that the FBI had told him that he should start wearing a flak jacket everywhere that he goes. It doesn’t surprise me at all.” Travis went on to reinforce that he had McAFee’s back through the supposedly frightening moment. “I just think I got Pat McAfee’s back on this. Now, if you want to argue, hey, individual videos, or you don’t need to be offended by them, everything else, I think you need to think about where his mind is. And I don’t think he’s crazy to have his mind there in a position that, when you’re in an outdoor venue, it is incredibly difficult to secure. And I feel like as someone who is on television there, you have no idea what’s going on around you,” he said. “You are a proverbial sitting duck.” The post ‘You are a proverbial sitting duck’: Clay Travis understands Pat McAfee’s fear after Charlie Kirk’s assassination appeared first on The Comeback: Today’s Top Sports Stories & Reactions .

item.title: Rilany Silva hails Brazil U17s' mindset after dramatic last-eight berth
item.description: Rilany Silva hails Brazil U17s' mindset after dramatic last-eight berth Brazil’s U-17 Women’s National Team’s qualification for the World Cup quarterfinals in Morocco on Wednesday (28) reinforced coach Rilany Silva’s confidence in the work being done with the team. Following a 3-3 draw with Poland in regulation time and a penalty shootout victory, the coach highlighted the players’ competitive mentality as one of Brazil’s key strengths in the tournament. For Rilany, their ability to stay composed in the face of adversity was crucial to overcoming the match’s twists and turns and securing a place in the next round. “What we’ve been emphasizing most with them is mentality. If we want to reach the top of the world, or get as close as possible, we need to start with our mentality. With every game, they’re showing that this is non-negotiable. Our mentality is our performance, and that’s what makes me happiest and most confident about what we’re doing and what we can achieve,” she said. The coach also stressed that the challenges may change with each match, but the team’s attitude must remain consistent until the end. She said the match against Poland was another demonstration of the squad’s mental strength. Brazil’s U-17 National Team celebrates reaching the World Cup quarterfinals in Morocco Credits: Fabio Souza / CBF “The game will change, the opponent will change, the challenges will change, but their mentality stays the same until the final whistle. Today was further proof of that. For them, since they sometimes have doubts about certain things, I think today’s game can serve as confirmation. This mentality will take us as far as possible,” she added. Brazil awaits its next opponent, which will be decided by the match between China and France. Aware of the different styles the two teams could bring, Rilany emphasized that Brazil’s preparations will remain focused on its own competitive identity. “We don’t have a confirmed opponent yet. It could be China, with one style of play, or France, with a completely different one. We’ll only find out tomorrow. I believe our mentality will guide us and be what sets us apart in this competition. If our mentality stays intact, we’re capable of competing in any match,” she concluded. item.title: Liverpool beat Chelsea on penalties yet again to secure Carabao Cup progress
item.description: Chelsea must have known their fate as soon as the last 16 tie at Anfield went to penalties. Four times they had faced Liverpool in a penalty shoot-out previously and four times they had lost. Make that five, after Wesley Fofana’s woeful attempt sailed high into the Kop and sent Andoni Iraola’s side into the Carabao Cup quarter finals. The defender was not the only culprit as Chelsea’s catalogue of penalty misery against Liverpool gained a new chapter to add to the 2007 Champions League semi final, the 2019 Uefa Super Cup final and the FA and League Cup finals of 2022. Emmanuel Emegha could have won it for Xabi Alonso’s visitors but his effort was saved superbly by Giorgi Mamardashvili. Continue reading...

item.title: Alessia Russo makes history with hat-trick as Arsenal cruise to Benfica win
item.description: Alessia Russo wrote herself into the history books once again as she became the highest English goal-scorer in the Women’s Champions League. Her hat-trick gave Arsenal a 3-0 win over Benfica to send the Gunners up to second in the league phase table. It is safe to say that Arsenal’s season has yet to fully burst into life. Struggles in front of goal, unforced errors and rather lackadaisical performances have defined the opening two months. Saturday’s north London derby win did, however, feel like it could be a springboard for some much-needed momentum, a gritty performance that could kickstart Renée Slegers’ side into life. item.title: Nketiah takes Crystal Palace past Fulham and earns Sage breathing space
item.description: “Can we play you every week?” chanted the Crystal Palace fans as they celebrated a fifth victory over Fulham on their own patch in the space of 18 months. Eddie Nketiah’s first-half goal against the run of play eased some of the growing pressure on Pierre Sage as Palace booked a third consecutive appearance in the quarter-finals of this competition. The good news for Sage is that Arsenal – who beat them on both of those occasions – have already been eliminated . However, he knows that Saturday’s game at Tottenham will have much more bearing on whether he is still around by the time it resumes in mid-December against Sunderland. For Álvaro Arbeloa, this was a disappointing setback after a couple of weeks of progress. Fulham haven’t beaten Palace here since January 2005 – a run of 10 matches – and will not get a better chance after Sage made 10 changes, including the inspired return of their captain, Dean Henderson, in goal. His save in injury time from Gonzalo García proved crucial and there were boos for Fulham at the final whistle. Continue reading...

item.description: Only Matt Busby and Alex Ferguson have truly succeeded in the Old Trafford hot seat with each casting uneasy shadows Should any football club fit the Great Man theory of history it is Manchester United. item.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
item.description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...

item.title: The horse that ushered in Manchester United’s tragic arc | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s plenty of blame to go around at Old Trafford. Like all downfalls it started with a seemingly small, unconnected moment Sign up for our free newsletter here And so here we are again, at that point as the nights draw in and Manchester United prepare to sack a manager . Autumn: season of mists, mellow fruitfulness and a crisis at Old Trafford. Sunday’s 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth , coming on the back of last week’s 4-1 reverse against Como, made clear what many had feared from the moment Michael Carrick was given the job on a permanent basis: that he isn’t up to it. But then, who could be? When you’ve burned through a long list of managers in 13 years, it’s perhaps worth considering whether the manager is really the problem. Could some blame perhaps go to the director of football, Jason Wilcox, or the chief executive, Omar Berrada, the people making the appointments? Or perhaps to Sir Jim Ratcliffe, the cost-cutting tax exile and minority shareholder with responsibility for sporting operations? Or to the Glazer family, who plunged the club into debt with a leveraged buyout in 2005 and have since made calamitous decision after calamitous decision, reducing the most successful club in English league history to a mid-table laughing stock with a roof that leaks symbolically ? It was really important and this was a great opportunity to try and turn it around.” It has taken seven games for the Gunners to secure their second league win of the season despite high hopes ahead of the new campaign and, while the result was a significant one, there is still a long way to go if Arsenal are to salvage anything from the most disappointing of starts. The performance against Tottenham was far from perfect and, in the first half in particular, sloppy and lacking fight. Tightening up their passing and harnessing the grit they found as they clung onto their lead towards the end of the match will be critical if they are to really kick on from this result. item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
